Continue the CrewCut work of the previous round and complete c for its evaluation run (the fixed pipeline on caminandes3-L1-0000-scr, smoke profile): the shot correspondence, judged by CrewCut's continuity judge on the `gemini` resource from the shot descriptions of the previous round, and with it every component of c the code computes for that run.

Where its code fails (for example the judge's request settings, which made every Gemini model return an empty answer in the previous round), adapt it so it works, keeping what the measure measures. Record each adaptation as data: what was changed, why, and what it changes in the result. A version of the benchmark that this world makes and can reproduce from its records is a good outcome. Nothing goes back to CrewCut.

Check that the judge, as adapted, tells a right description from a wrong one, with a small check. Record the requests made to Gemini, by purpose, with the token usage the responses report, and the cost where a price is known.

Deliver: the completed c with each component and how it was computed, the adaptations, the judge check, the spend, and an updated statement of what was not run.

Budget: 20 turns and 900 model seconds for this world, within an hour of wall clock; at most 40 requests to Gemini.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Build and evaluate with CrewCut, the benchmark whose code and protocol are in the read-only `crewcut` resource and whose published dataset is in the read-only `crewcut-dataset` resource (`ht-resource list`, `ht-resource describe <id>`). Read CrewCut's README.md, its Issue #3 (`crewcut-issue-3.md`: what the Breakdown and the evaluation must do and deliver) and `.agents/memory/project/agentic-pipelines.md` in the code first. Install the code with pip, its core only.

This round is small: each of the two pipelines goes one stretch.

1. Breakdown, only the dev film Caminandes 3 (2.5 minutes, 37 shots, no dialogue): from the catalogue query to its task packages (find the candidate and read its licence for this film only, fetch the pinned master from its source and check its sha256 against `configs/films.yaml`, then shots, dialogue, hierarchy, provenance if feasible, tasks). Compare the result with the published dataset at revision d509bed: cuts, dialogue, hierarchy, task ids and fields. List every difference and explain it.
2. Shot descriptions: draft the description of every shot of the film with CrewCut's own describe step, on the `gemini` resource, and record the model that drafted them.
3. Evaluation, one of those tasks (for example caminandes3-L1-0000-scr) run with the fixed pipeline (`--system fixed --profile smoke`, the placeholder generator), scored to a complete c: the delivery check (Q), cut F1, shot correspondence judged through CrewCut's continuity judge on the `gemini` resource from those descriptions, and every other component of c the code computes for that run. The film has no dialogue, so WER and line-onset error do not apply: record them as not applicable. A component that cannot be computed is marked "not run" with the reason, without a conclusion.
4. The spend: the requests made to Gemini, by purpose, with the token usage the responses report, and the cost where a price is known (CrewCut's `configs/prices.yaml` or the provider's published price, with its source and date).

The real generators (T0), screening and the score S are out of this round: mark them "not run".

Judgment (finding the source, reading the licence, choosing the file to pin, what to do after a failure) is done by agents and recorded as data; the benchmark's commands are reproducible steps and checks. Do not change CrewCut's fixed configuration or protocol; a gap or inconsistency in its documents, and every decision Issue #3 leaves open, belongs to CrewCut's maintainer: record it, do not choose. Nothing goes back to CrewCut.

Deliver: the benchmark files and records (decisions as data, commands run with their outcomes, the comparison with each difference explained, the descriptions with their model, the evaluation result with each component of c and how it was computed, the spend), and a statement of what was not run.

Budget: 60 turns and 3600 model seconds for the whole world, within two hours of wall clock; at most 150 requests to Gemini.

The maintainer has decided, for this and later rounds: CrewCut's code is not binding where it does not work here; CrewCut will change too. Where its code fails (for example the judge's request settings, which made every Gemini model return an empty answer in the previous round), adapt it so it works, keeping what the measure measures. issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Build and evaluate with CrewCut, the benchmark whose code and protocol are in the read-only `crewcut` resource and whose published dataset is in the read-only `crewcut-dataset` resource (`ht-resource list`, `ht-resource describe <id>`). Read CrewCut's README.md, its Issue #3 (`crewcut-issue-3.md`: what the Breakdown and the evaluation must do and deliver) and `.agents/memory/project/agentic-pipelines.md` in the code first. Install the code with pip, its core only.

This round is small: each of the two pipelines goes one stretch.

1. Breakdown, only the dev film Caminandes 3 (2.5 minutes, 37 shots, no dialogue): from the catalogue query to its task packages (find the candidate and read its licence for this film only, fetch the pinned master from its source and check its sha256 against `configs/films.yaml`, then shots, dialogue, hierarchy, provenance if feasible, tasks). Compare the result with the published dataset at revision d509bed: cuts, dialogue, hierarchy, task ids and fields. List every difference and explain it.
2. Shot descriptions: draft the description of every shot of the film with CrewCut's own describe step, on the `gemini` resource, and record the model that drafted them.
3. Evaluation, one of those tasks (for example caminandes3-L1-0000-scr) run with the fixed pipeline (`--system fixed --profile smoke`, the placeholder generator), scored to a complete c: the delivery check (Q), cut F1, shot correspondence judged through CrewCut's continuity judge on the `gemini` resource from those descriptions, and every other component of c the code computes for that run. The film has no dialogue, so WER and line-onset error do not apply: record them as not applicable. A component that cannot be computed is marked "not run" with the reason, without a conclusion.
4. The spend: the requests made to Gemini, by purpose, with the token usage the responses report, and the cost where a price is known (CrewCut's `configs/prices.yaml` or the provider's published price, with its source and date).

The real generators (T0), screening and the score S are out of this round: mark them "not run".

Judgment (finding the source, reading the licence, choosing the file to pin, what to do after a failure) is done by agents and recorded as data; the benchmark's commands are reproducible steps and checks. Do not change CrewCut's fixed configuration or protocol; a gap or inconsistency in its documents, and every decision Issue #3 leaves open, belongs to CrewCut's maintainer: record it, do not choose. Nothing goes back to CrewCut.

Deliver: the benchmark files and records (decisions as data, commands run with their outcomes, the comparison with each difference explained, the descriptions with their model, the evaluation result with each component of c and how it was computed, the spend), and a statement of what was not run.

Budget: 60 turns and 3600 model seconds for the whole world, within two hours of wall clock; at most 150 requests to Gemini.
